div.div:
• common entry point -- a fresh ADR is usually logged here first.
•• common end point -- log directly here for historical documentation.
*Completed work and anything explicitly spelled out in the QEMU Action Plan (AP) are taken as whole when considering what is deferred or incorporated into the project, so there are two senses of each term. Deferred could be something that was skipped or stubbed out when the phase was completed, or it is something in a future phase that was unknown / unidentified when the AP was written, or now needs to be changed. Incorporated means it was either implemented, or is in AP to be implemented.
Child ADRs: whenever a self-contained piece of an ADR needs its own tracking, it spawns a child ADR. If it is to transition a subset of the parent, spawn the child and transition it the same way the parent would have. If there is any functional or contextual dependency, ADRs should cite their parent/children explicitly.
Bugs: any time a bug is found, track it a separate ADR. Bugs may be linked to parent and/or child ADRs that create, exhibit, or fix the bug. Bugs are behavioural descriptions only and stay open until the behaviour is verified to be fixed (closed) or noted as intended (transition to note). If it is unable to be replicated, document the efforts and close it.
Superseding: any decision can be superseded when a better approach is found; the superseded ADR remains for historical context, and gains a pointer to its replacement. Shown once from incorporated -- the common case.
